source.citation: Luo MM, Usmani SZ, Mateos MV, Nahi H, Chari A, San-Miguel J, Touzeau C, Suzuki K, Kaiser M, Carson R, Heuck C, Qi M, Zhou H, Sun YN, Parasrampuria DA. Exposure-response and population pharmacokinetic analyses of a novel subcutaneous formulation of daratumumab administered to multiple myeloma patients. J Clin Pharmacol. 2021;61(5):614-627.
source.licence: Open access, CC BY-NC (stated on the article's first page).
source.storage: Kept on the platform owner's computer only; not committed.
source.extraction: AI-assisted from the article text layer and the Word document XML of Table S1. Independent review pending.

structure.description: Two-compartment model with parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten (saturable, target-mediated) elimination from the central compartment; the maximum rate of the saturable pathway decreases over time; subcutaneous doses enter through a depot with first-order absorption and bioavailability F1 (Introduction and Methods, PopPK Analyses, article pages 615-616).

compartments.central: volume V1; linear clearance CL; saturable elimination Vmax, Km

equations: dA1/dt = R_iv(t) + Ka Adepot - CL C - Vmax(t) C / (Km + C) - Q (C - A2/V2),  C = A1 / V1
Vmax(t) = Vmax exp(-KDES t), t = time since the first dose
structure.equations_basis: Not printed in the article or supplement. The text describes the structure (2 compartments, parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten elimination, a decrease of total target over time) and Table S1 names KDES 'first-order rate for decrease of Vmax'; the exponential form is the standard reading of that definition and is an assumption here. The earlier intravenous model (Xu et al., ref 24) was not reviewed.
structure.units: Amounts mg, volumes L, clearances L/h, Vmax mg/h, Km ug/mL (= mg/L); concentration mg/L = ug/mL.

parameters.location: Table S1 (JCPH-61-614-s003.docx), 'Parameter Estimates of the popPK Model of DARA Based on Combined DARA SC and DARA IV Data'
parameters.covariate_equations_as_printed: TVCLj=0.00496*Bwj78.61.24*ALBj37-1.85*TPMMCL, where TPMMCL is a shift factor of 1 for non-IgG subjects with multiple myeloma and 1+1.26 for IgG subjects with multiple myeloma. TVV1j=5.25*BWj78.60.91*SEXV1, where SEXV1 is a shift factor of 1 for female and 1 to 0.105 for male. (Table S1 note; superscripts and the operator lost in the document text.)

covariate_equations_read.cl: CL = 0.00496 x (WT / 78.6 kg)^1.24 x (ALB / 37 g/L)^-1.85 x (2.26 if IgG myeloma else 1)
notes: Albumin in g/L (Table 2 reports albumin in g/L, median 38-41).
The IgG shift is stated as '1+1.26', i.e. IgG myeloma clearance 2.26 times non-IgG.
The sex factor for males is printed as '1 to 0.105'; read as 1 - 0.105 (= 0.895) from the estimate -0.105. The direction (which sex is the reference) rests on this reading of a garbled line; open.

random_effects.form: Table S1 column 'IIV (%CV)'; correlations between random effects not reported (none assumed).

residual_error.note: Not used by the platform (measurement and misspecification noise).

data_used_to_build.location: Abstract; Methods, PopPK Analyses (article page 616); Table 1 (page 617)
data_used_to_build.earlier_model: Structure and covariates were carried over from the earlier intravenous population model (Xu et al., ref 24; Clin Pharmacokinet 2017), which was built on GEN501 and SIRIUS. Luo re-estimated all parameters on the four studies above. GEN501 and SIRIUS data are therefore not in this model's parameter estimates but did inform its form.

population.location: Table 2, article page 619 (weight distribution not tabulated; abstract gives the range)

summary_values_stated.steady_state: about 5 months after the first dose of the every-4-week schedule

limitations: The time course of Vmax (KDES) is read as exponential decay; the form is not printed.
The sex factor on V1 is read from a garbled line; the reference sex is uncertain.
No correlations between random effects are reported.
Renal and hepatic function were tested and not retained; the population had eGFR down to about 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 and mostly normal liver function (Table 2).
